chapter: Will Vodery and the road shows
title: How Whaley first became a show director in Philadelphia
summary: He explains Lee Whipper made him direct the show while Mrs. Nicholas played piano and Mr. Nicholas drums, and they straighten out the 1920s timeline.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: I used to conduct the show. That's -- I started when the Nicholas -- Mrs. Nicholas, she -- I was supposed to play the piano, see. I wasn't supposed to direct it. And I told the man -- he said, you go on and direct the show.
Lee Whippet was this great movie star, one of our first great-name movie stars.
Yeah. And Lee says, you direct and she will play the piano. Okay, I said.
Well, did he produce it or --
Yeah, and Mr. Nichols, he played drums.
Yeah. Now, we go back to 1940, 1950.
Let's see, we're back in the '20s now.
We're at the '20s in Pittsburgh. Because Mr. Nichols and them wasn't around in the '50s.

No. We're coming out of the -- that's Stopping the Traffic. And they put the man in the hospital and we went on to Chicago, St. Louis and then back to Chicago and on to Pittsburgh, and you know, the route, the TOBA circuit. Now, let me say, after I come out with Duke, see, in '40.
